items.headline: First 62.5bn-yuan trade-in fund batch for 2026 allocated
items.driver: Ultra-long special treasury bonds allocated early to keep the consumer goods trade-in scheme running into 2026.
items.customer_relevance: Subsidies keep supporting replacement demand, but mostly favour cheaper cars via %-of-price caps; little direct pull for 5/7 Series buyers.
items.quote: China has allocated 62.5 billion yuan (HK$69.6 billion)
items.notes: Covers all consumer goods, not only cars. Article notes total 2026 size not specified; 2025 had 300bn yuan.

items.headline: Second 62.5bn-yuan batch; 2026 trade-in total set at 250bn yuan
items.driver: NDRC released the second batch of ultra-long special treasury bond funds; annual plan 250bn yuan vs 300bn in 2025.
items.customer_relevance: Smaller total pot than 2025 means subsidy-driven demand weakens; buyers become more value-sensitive.
items.quote: a total of 250 billion yuan in ultra-long special treasury bonds to support trade-in programs in 2026.
items.notes: Second batch: 'the second batch of funds raised through such bonds for the programs this year.' 2025 comparison (300bn) from The Standard.

items.headline: Over 11.5 million cars traded in under 2025 subsidy scheme
items.driver: National scrappage/replacement subsidies drove trade-ins through 2025 (to 28 Dec).
items.customer_relevance: A large share of 2025 purchases were subsidy-pulled; some demand pulled forward from 2026.
items.quote: 截至2025年12月28日，2025年汽车以旧换新超1150万辆，带动新车销售额超1.6万亿元。
items.notes: Gloss: by 28 Dec 2025, over 11.5m vehicles traded in, driving >1.6 trillion yuan of new-car sales.

items.headline: Only 612k cars traded in by 19 Feb 2026
items.driver: Slow start of 2026 scheme (new %-of-price rules, local rollout) per CCTV data.
items.customer_relevance: Weak early-2026 subsidy uptake matches the January sales dip; demand less policy-driven than 2025.
items.quote: 汽车以旧换新 61.2 万辆，带动新车销售额 1005.3 亿元
items.notes: Gloss: 612k car trade-ins, 100.5bn yuan new-car sales, cumulative to 19 Feb 2026. Not comparable to full-year 2025 figure; no H1 2026 total found.

items.headline: 20+ Chinese cities paused or adjusted car trade-in subsidies
items.driver: Local subsidy quotas ran out late in 2025, so cities paused or changed application rules (Yicai partial tally).
items.customer_relevance: Subsidy availability is patchy by city; buyers time purchases around quota windows.
items.quote: 据第一财经不完全统计，截至目前，全国已有超20个地市陆续暂停或调整了汽车以旧换新补贴申请。
items.notes: Gloss: by Yicai's incomplete count, over 20 prefecture-level cities have paused or adjusted car trade-in subsidy applications. Unit = cities.

items.headline: 2026 trade-in quotas tight in Guangdong, Zhejiang; first-come rules
items.driver: Fixed provincial pots with 'quota management' and first-come-first-served rules; Zhejiang ~60% spent by April.
items.customer_relevance: Subsidy uncertainty again by region in 2026; premium buyers largely unaffected by caps but dealers lose a sales lever.
items.quote: 资金用尽后不再受理新申请
items.notes: Gloss: once funds are used up, no new applications are accepted (Zhejiang). Also Guangdong '补贴已经面临额度紧张问题'. T3 aggregator; no official list of 2026 pauses found.

items.headline: 2026 trade-in rules: monthly-balanced funds, payout within 30 workdays
items.driver: Ministries' 2026 implementation rules spread funds month by month to avoid 2025-style mid-year stoppages.
items.customer_relevance: Intended to smooth subsidy availability through the year.
items.quote: 2026年汽车以旧换新补贴资金按月均衡使用
items.notes: Gloss: 2026 car trade-in funds to be used evenly month by month. Value = 30 working days to pay out ('30个工作日内兑付补贴'). Signed 30 Dec 2025.

items.headline: NBS consumer confidence 89.6, highest in almost three years
items.driver: Gradual improvement from 2022 lows, but still below 100 (pessimistic territory).
items.customer_relevance: Households still cautious; premium purchases face value scrutiny.
items.quote: the NBS consumer confidence index edged up to 89.6 in September, the highest score in almost 3 years.
items.notes: Index >100 = optimism. Dec 2025 reading not found with a citable dated source.

items.headline: China consumer confidence stuck near 89 in mid-2026
items.driver: No driver given; reading flat versus late 2025.
items.customer_relevance: No recovery in household sentiment; buyers keep prioritising value and discounts.
items.quote: Consumer Confidence in China decreased to 89.20 points in July from 89.40 points in June of 2026.
items.notes: Aggregator labels source as OECD; series looks like the NBS index. Exact publication date of the June value unknown (published_at is an estimate; may have been released after the cut-off) and July 89.2 was certainly released after 31 Jul - treat as indicative only.

items.headline: China mandates AEB as standard on light vehicles from 2028
items.driver: MIIT issued GB 39901-2025, China's first mandatory driver-assist standard (approved 31 Dec 2025).
items.customer_relevance: Basic active safety becomes table stakes; differentiation moves to NOA quality and HMI.
items.quote: AEB systems become standard equipment for light-duty vehicles
items.notes: Takes effect 1 Jan 2028.

items.headline: Mandatory L2/NOA safety standard GB 47955-2026 issued, effective 2027
items.driver: SAMR/SAC approved first mandatory safety baseline for combined driver assistance incl. NOA after rapid adoption.
items.customer_relevance: NOA becomes regulated: driver monitoring, warnings and data recording will shape how BMW's assist features feel.
items.quote: 《智能网联汽车 组合驾驶辅助系统安全要求》（GB 47955—2026）
items.notes: Gloss: 'Intelligent connected vehicles - safety requirements for combined driver assistance systems'. '拟于2027年1月1日起正式实施' (effective 1 Jan 2027). MIIT approval date reported as 27 Jun 2026.

items.headline: L2 standard: hands/eyes monitoring, 72h NOA road tests, 2028 for existing models
items.driver: Standard requires continuous driver monitoring and escalating warnings; new types from 2027, in-production types from 2028.
items.customer_relevance: Successor 5/7 Series NOA must pass hands/gaze monitoring; nag-free hands-off feel restricted.
items.quote: 系统在激活状态下需持续监测驾驶员手部和视线状态。
items.notes: Gloss: when active, the system must continuously monitor the driver's hands and gaze. Value = '领航组合驾驶辅助（NOA）功能需开展累计不少于72小时的有效道路试验' (>=72 h road tests). Data recording (DSSCDA) mandatory; accident-data part delayed 1 year.

items.headline: 64% of China's new passenger cars had combined driver assistance in 2025
items.driver: MIIT data cited alongside the AEB standard.
items.customer_relevance: L2 is mainstream; premium buyers expect at least capable L2, increasingly NOA.
items.quote: combined driver assistance functions, including AEB systems
items.notes: Value 64% reported by fetch summary in sentence with this phrase; exact full sentence not captured verbatim.

items.headline: L2 in 70% of new cars in 2026; NOA-equipped above 30%
items.driver: Government figures cited at release of GB 47955-2026.
items.customer_relevance: NOA is now a mainstream expectation in China; lacking urban NOA is a visible gap.
items.quote: 2026年以来，我国搭载组合驾驶辅助功能的乘用车新车市场渗透率达到70%
items.notes: Gloss: since start of 2026, new-passenger-car penetration of combined driver assistance reached 70%; '配备领航驾驶辅助功能（NOA）的车型渗透率超过30%' (NOA >30%). Compare existing items china-noa-penetration-h1-2026 (34.2%) and china-l3-operating-l2-penetration-h1-2026 (70.5%).

items.headline: China regulators plan ban on fully retractable door handles
items.driver: Draft mandatory door-handle standard after safety concerns with electronic-only handles.
items.customer_relevance: Flush/hidden handles become a liability in China; mechanical backup needed.
items.quote: Enforcement is anticipated to begin in July 2027.
items.notes: Draft: 'a direct ban on fully retractable handles, with a one-year transition period.' Final rule (Feb 2026) set 1 Jan 2027.

items.headline: China bans hidden door handles from 2027; existing models by 2029
items.driver: MIIT mandatory standard after fatal incidents where electronic doors would not open (e.g. Xiaomi SU7 fire).
items.customer_relevance: Successor designs for China need visible mechanical inner and outer handles; affects flush-handle design language.
items.quote: revise their designs to comply with the new requirements by January 2029.
items.notes: Effective 'on January 1, 2027' for new approvals. Vehicles must 'be equipped with mechanical exterior door handles and interior door handles' (tailgate excepted).

items.headline: BMW 735Li China list price cut to 808,000 yuan
items.driver: BMW repriced 31 models from 1 Jan 2026 to counter fierce competition.
items.customer_relevance: 7 Series entry now under the 900k-yuan luxury consumption-tax line; value-for-money matters even in luxury.
items.quote: The entry-level 735Li now starts at 808,000 yuan (115,400 USD), down from 919,000 yuan (131,300 USD)
items.notes: Link to 900k-yuan luxury-tax threshold (item cn-luxury-consumption-tax) is our assumption, not stated by source. 5 Series ICE prices not listed in this article.

items.headline: BMW i7 M70L China price cut by 301,000 yuan
items.driver: Part of BMW's 1 Jan 2026 China price reset across 31 models.
items.customer_relevance: Electric luxury sedans need strong value case vs. Maextro S800 and others.
items.quote: the premium i7 M70L electric sedan has been reduced by 301,000 yuan (43,000 USD)
items.notes: From 1,899,000 to 1,598,000 yuan per article table. See existing bmw-i7-cn-discontinued-2026.

items.headline: BMW China BEV sales ~53,000 in 2025, under 10% of total
items.driver: German luxury brands lag domestic Chinese brands in electrification pace; BMW guided suppliers to <500k local output in 2026.
items.customer_relevance: BMW's China customer base is still ICE-heavy; EV credibility must be built with Neue Klasse.
items.quote: accounted for less than 10% of its total sales.
items.notes: Total 2025: 'BMW sold 625,527 units, down 12.5% year-on-year.' 2026 local-production forecast to suppliers below 500,000 units.

items.headline: J.D. Power China sales satisfaction falls; premium 762, Land Rover top
items.driver: Shoppers better informed via apps/media; online experience lowest-scoring factor; rejector satisfaction dropped 24 points.
items.customer_relevance: Premium buyers expect seamless online-to-showroom journeys and expert test drives.
items.quote: premium and mass market brands score 762 and 757 points, respectively, declining 5 and 2 points year over year.
items.notes: Industry 758. 'Land Rover ranks highest among premium brands with a score of 775. Audi (772) ranks second. Porsche (767) ranks third.' BMW not in top 3. 2026 successor study appears to be PXI (see jdp-cn-pxi-2026-premium).

items.headline: 40% of China buyers say salesperson's test-drive expertise decided purchase
items.driver: Shorter decision cycles; 76.4% arrive with a model in mind; test drive increasingly decisive.
items.customer_relevance: Features must be demonstrable in a short test drive; explainable tech wins.
items.quote: 40% of buyers say the professionalism of the salesperson during the test drive had the greatest impact on their decision, up 4.5 percentage points from 2024.
items.notes: yoy_pct here is percentage points.

items.headline: 21.4% of ICE buyers considered an NEV; half rejected before showroom
items.driver: Rejections increasingly due to dealers (slow response, poor needs understanding, no stock).
items.customer_relevance: ICE-loyal premium buyers are open to NEVs but need convincing offers and dealer competence.
items.quote: The proportion of ICE vehicle owners considering new energy vehicles (NEVs) has risen to 21.4% this year from 15.7% in 2024.
items.notes: 50.2% of them rejected the purchase before the in-store viewing phase (42.2% in 2024).

items.headline: J.D. Power China service satisfaction: premium 798, Land Rover leads
items.driver: NEV makers push efficient, transparent digital processes; WeChat and membership channels build loyalty.
items.customer_relevance: Premium owners expect digital, transparent after-sales service.
items.quote: Direct engagement channels such as WeChat and exclusive membership systems are continuously building user loyalty.
items.notes: Scores (industry 789, premium 798 +2; Land Rover 809, Mercedes-Benz 808, Cadillac 804) from fetch summary; quote verbatim. BMW not named in top 3.

items.headline: J.D. Power China service satisfaction: premium up 11 to 809
items.driver: Digital appointment usage rising; app/WeChat mini-program use for maintenance up 1.8x in two years.
items.customer_relevance: Self-service digital booking and instant confirmation are becoming expected after-sales features.
items.quote: improving 11 points year over year to 809 points
items.notes: Industry 794 (+5). Top premium: Land Rover 819, Mercedes-Benz 813, Audi 812; BMW not named. ICE owners only.

items.headline: 44.7% of China service visits now booked digitally
items.driver: Growing use of apps/mini-programs; unmet demand for self-chosen slots and instant confirmation widens gaps.
items.customer_relevance: Car apps must offer seamless service booking; part of the digital brand experience.
items.quote: Mobile App/WeChat Mini-Program usage for maintenance inquiries has surged 1.8 times in 2 years
items.notes: 44.7% (+1.1 pp) from fetch summary; quote is from page as relayed. yoy in pp.

items.headline: 69% of Chinese buyers call advanced assisted driving a must-have
items.driver: McKinsey 2026 China Auto Consumer Survey: ADAS and in-car AI becoming expected features.
items.customer_relevance: Capable NOA is a baseline expectation for successor 5 Series LWB buyers in China.
items.quote: 69 percent of respondents now consider advanced assisted-driving features
items.notes: Survey launched 12 May 2026 (McKinsey China). Not premium-specific. McKinsey 2025 equivalent figure not retrieved (page timed out).

items.headline: 84% expect in-car AI to go beyond voice commands
items.driver: McKinsey 2026 survey: in-car AI expected to evolve into proactive digital companions.
items.customer_relevance: AI assistant quality (proactive, conversational) is a key cockpit requirement in China.
items.quote: 84 percent said they expect in-car AI assistants to evolve beyond simple voice-command systems

items.headline: Brand now second-most important EV purchase factor in China
items.driver: Price war causing hesitation rather than sales; buyers shift from price to value and brand credibility.
items.customer_relevance: Opportunity for BMW brand heritage if paired with competitive tech.
items.quote: 'brand' rose to become the second-most important purchase factor for electric vehicles
items.notes: Value = rank 2.

items.headline: Tech upgrades add net 20.7% to purchase intent; price war seen negatively
items.driver: 22.2% of recent buyers view price war negatively vs 16.5% positively.
items.customer_relevance: Real feature upgrades move buyers more than discounts.
items.quote: technology upgrades and improved features generated a net positive effect of 20.7 percent on purchase intentions
items.notes: A McKinsey partner's LinkedIn post says this is nearly double the 2025 level (not verified).

items.headline: NEV discounts averaged 13.7% of sticker price in Q1 2026
items.driver: Ongoing price competition; ~70 NEV models across premium, JV and domestic brands discounted (CPCA).
items.customer_relevance: Transaction prices far below list; perceived value per yuan is critical.
items.quote: Average price cuts reached 38,000 yuan ($5,300), or 13.7 percent of sticker prices.
items.notes: Gasoline cars: 'average discounts of 37,000 yuan, or 14.3 percent.' Also: PV sales -18.5% yoy in first four months.

items.headline: BMW to put Alibaba Qwen-based AI assistant in China Neue Klasse from 2026
items.driver: Expanded BMW-Alibaba partnership to localise the Intelligent Personal Assistant for Chinese users.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese buyers expect LLM-grade conversational assistants; BMW's answer is local partners.
items.quote: The AI-enhanced IPA will debut in BMW Neue Klasse models produced in China starting from 2026.
items.notes: Two agents: 'the Car Genius, an onboard expert for vehicle functions and real-time assistance' and 'the Travel Companion'.

items.headline: China iX3 LWB: Alibaba LLM, DeepSeek, HarmonyOS/HiCar, Momenta NOA
items.driver: BMW tailors software and AI for China with local partners.
items.customer_relevance: Shows the China feature bar BMW itself set: local LLM, phone ecosystem integration, urban NOA.
items.quote: local travel scenarios across both highway and urban roads
items.notes: AI/HarmonyOS details from fetch summary; only the quoted phrase confirmed verbatim. Overlaps existing bmw-ix3-lwb-reveal-mar-2026 (Jing Daily).

items.headline: BMW and Momenta co-develop China driver assist for new iX3
items.driver: End-to-end AI models adapted to China's traffic; testing at four bases.
items.customer_relevance: Local ADAS partner needed to match Chinese NOA expectations.
items.quote: the driving assistance system jointly developed by BMW and Momenta
items.notes: Testing in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenyang, Nanjing; production at BMW Brilliance Shenyang in 2026.

items.headline: China iX3 LWB filed: 3,005 mm wheelbase, urban and highway NOA
items.driver: Sales licence filing; car stretched 103 mm vs global version.
items.customer_relevance: Rear legroom stretch plus urban NOA is BMW's China formula; relevant for 5 Series LWB successor.
items.quote: capable of the Navigate On Autopilot (NOA) function on urban roads and highways
items.notes: Value = wheelbase in mm. Dimensions 4885/1895/1635 mm.

items.headline: China iX3 LWB rated 919 km CLTC, 400 km in 10 minutes
items.driver: MIIT filing data; 13.6 kWh/100 km consumption.
items.customer_relevance: Range and 10-minute fast charging are BMW's claim against Chinese EV rivals.
items.quote: recover 400 km of range in just 10 minutes of fast charging
items.notes: 'CLTC pure electric range of 919 km'; 17.9-inch touchscreen, 3D HUD, thicker/longer rear cushions; deliveries Q4 2026.

items.headline: BMW has 480+ local Tier-1 suppliers for China iX3 LWB
items.driver: Chinese innovation partners involved earlier and deeper in development and validation.
items.customer_relevance: Local development speed should bring China-specific features faster.
items.quote: 目前，宝马在中国拥有超过480家本土一级供应商
items.notes: Gloss: BMW currently has over 480 local Tier-1 suppliers in China. Also '中国创新伙伴正更早、更深地参与宝马产品开发、技术验证和量产准备'.

items.headline: Tesla China adopts DeepSeek and Doubao for voice assistant
items.driver: Even Tesla localises in-car AI with Chinese LLMs for the Model Y L.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese LLMs are the expected basis for cockpit voice AI in China.
items.quote: Tesla has introduced a voice-activated in-car virtual assistant for the first time in the Model Y L.
items.notes: Doubao for commands, DeepSeek for chat. Total brand count of DeepSeek integrations not found (see existing china-deepseek-cockpit-integrations).

items.headline: Tesla rolls Doubao voice assistant to China cars; Qwen testing
items.driver: OTA 2026.14.13; DeepSeek for chat, Alibaba Qwen reportedly near launch.
items.customer_relevance: Multi-LLM cockpit assistants are becoming standard even outside Chinese brands.
items.quote: It doesn't just chat — it can also sing, debate and tell stories,
items.notes: Quote is Tesla's Weibo post.

items.headline: Geely and StepFun launch AI-agent cockpit with emotion detection
items.driver: Industry push to agent-based, emotionally responsive cockpits (WAIC 2025).
items.customer_relevance: Chinese buyers will compare BMW's assistant with emotional, memory-aware agents.
items.quote: more natural, more human, and more emotional new cockpit interaction experience
items.notes: First in Geely Galaxy M9.

items.headline: ByteDance and Seres put ~30B-parameter AI model on the car
items.driver: Doubao entering cabins; on-vehicle full-domain perception model on Nvidia Thor chips.
items.customer_relevance: Next-gen cockpits run large on-board AI; raises bar for BMW's assistant latency and capability.
items.quote: deploying a massive model with around 30 billion parameters on the vehicle side
items.notes: Value = billion parameters.

items.headline: Mercedes puts Zhipu multimodal AI in new Maybach for China
items.driver: Fierce competition; AI added to attract tech-savvy Chinese luxury buyers, incl. rear entertainment.
items.customer_relevance: Direct 7 Series rival offers local multimodal AI in rear entertainment; benchmark for G70 successor.
items.quote: multimodal large language model technology, co-developed by Mercedes, Tsinghua University, and Zhipu
items.notes: Rear entertainment system 'will integrate natural language processing'.

items.headline: Mercedes China electric GLC: 3,027 mm LWB, 39.1in screen, Doubao, Momenta
items.driver: Extensive localisation for Chinese buyers.
items.customer_relevance: German rival's China formula: long wheelbase, huge screen, local LLM, local ADAS.
items.quote: has been adapted to work with Doubao, the AI large language model owned by ByteDance
items.notes: '39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen'; Momenta ADAS; 800V, 10-80% in 22 min; wheelbase +55 mm.

items.headline: Audi A5L launched with Huawei driver assist incl. urban NOA
items.driver: German JV brand adopts Huawei Qiankun ADS to compete in China.
items.customer_relevance: Even ICE premium cars in China now offer urban NOA from local suppliers.
items.quote: advanced driver-assistance features such as urban NOA (Navigate on Autopilot), highway NOA, and advanced parking
items.notes: Q5L with Huawei ADAS followed on 15 Jan 2026 at 309,800 yuan.

items.headline: New Audi A6L: 3,066 mm wheelbase, starts 323,000 yuan, far below old list
items.driver: Pre-sales opened 10 Mar 2026; priced ~105-123k yuan below old model's MSRP.
items.customer_relevance: Direct 5 Series LWB rival resets price/space expectations; passenger screen now standard fare.
items.quote: The A6L starts at "323,000 yuan (46,740 USD)."
items.notes: Quote reconstructed from fetch summary; verbatim fragment is '323,000 yuan (46,740 USD)'. Screens 11.9+14.5+10.9 in; old MSRP 427,900-558,900 yuan (pre-discount).

items.headline: BYD cars with God's Eye driver assist pass 2 million
items.driver: BYD made ADAS standard across its range in 2025.
items.customer_relevance: Driver assistance is democratised; premium must offer clearly better NOA.
items.quote: vehicles equipped with its God's Eye smart driving system have surpassed cumulative sales of 2 million units

items.headline: BYD takes full liability for urban NOA accidents; 3.15m ADAS cars
items.driver: BYD expands smart-driving push with one-year accident liability guarantee for God's Eye A/B users.
items.customer_relevance: Liability guarantees raise trust expectations for NOA; premium brands may need similar assurances.
items.quote: will assume full financial liability for traffic accidents caused by its urban navigate-on-autopilot system in China.
items.notes: 3.15m = BYD vehicles with assisted driving systems (not only God's Eye) as of late May 2026.

items.headline: Huawei ADS option effectively rises to 15,000 yuan from July
items.driver: Chip price increases; >10 automakers raised prices or cut discounts on ADAS options.
items.customer_relevance: Chinese buyers do pay for premium NOA packages; signals willingness-to-pay for advanced ADAS.
items.quote: the price users actually pay will climb to 15,000 yuan
items.notes: List price 36,000 yuan; OEM subsidies ~20,000 yuan.

items.headline: China EV charging plugs exceed 20 million at end-2025
items.driver: NEA data; private plugs +56.2%, public +31.9% yoy.
items.customer_relevance: Charging anxiety fading; fast-charging speed matters more than availability.
items.quote: exceeded the 20 million mark, reaching 20.092 million
items.notes: Public 4.717m, private 15.375m; avg public charger power ~46.53 kW.

items.headline: Dongfeng joins BYD with 1,500 kW chargers; Hongqi 10-70% in 3m41s
items.driver: Megawatt flash charging race spreads beyond BYD to state-owned OEMs.
items.customer_relevance: 5-minute charging becoming a China benchmark; 10-minute 400 km claims may look average by 2028-30.
items.quote: 10% to 70% SOC in just 3 minutes and 41 seconds
items.notes: Dongfeng 'single-gun peak power of 1,500 kW'. BYD gen-2 flash charger also 1,500 kW (Mar 2026). Huawei/Zeekr/CATL Shenxing items not retrieved.

items.headline: Porsche to close all ~200 own charging stations in China
items.driver: Changing market conditions and user charging habits.
items.customer_relevance: Brand-owned charging is not a must for premium buyers if public fast charging is dense.
items.quote: As market conditions evolve and user charging habits continue to change
items.notes: Closures from 1 Mar 2026. Value = stations.

items.headline: Seres joins BMW-Mercedes premium charging JV Ionchi
items.driver: JV aims for 1,000 supercharging stations by end-2026; 430 stations / 2,408 points in 37 cities at Dec 2025.
items.customer_relevance: BMW keeps a premium charging offer in China, unlike Porsche; supports EV ownership experience.
items.quote: 430 supercharging stations, providing 2,408 charging points across 37 cities
items.notes: Each of BMW Brilliance, Mercedes, Seres holds one-third.

items.headline: BMW recalls 7,740 EVs incl. i7 and i5 in China
items.driver: Risk of erroneous high-voltage system shutdowns.
items.customer_relevance: Quality/reliability perception of BMW EVs in China at stake.
items.quote: erroneous shutdowns of the high-voltage system under specific operating conditions
items.notes: Models: i7, iX, i5, iX1, i3.

items.headline: BMW recalls ~180,000 5/7 Series and M5 in China over wiring
items.driver: Improperly routed A/C wiring harness can be damaged at filter change, fire risk (SAMR).
items.customer_relevance: Hits core 5 Series LWB owners; quality perception and service experience matter.
items.quote: totals 179,527 vehicles
items.notes: 'Affected models include domestically produced and imported 5 Series, 7 Series, and M5.' Separate 147,830-unit import recall (starter motor) reported by CarNewsChina 12 Mar 2026 (not fetched).
